propositions: CPython 3.12+ emits DeprecationWarning when fork() is called in multithreaded hosts, and Python 3.14 no longer defaults to fork, making the hard-coded fork context in the grounding harness unsafe.
The grounding worker harness hard-codes POSIX fork context via multiprocessing.get_context('fork'), which is reached by run_in_worker and causes deadlock risk when background threads exist.
Worker callables must be importable module-level names with pickleable args/kwargs/returns to support spawn-based multiprocessing, ruling out dynamic closures and lambdas.
Process start failures, pickling failures, parent receive failures, and unpickling failures must return fail-open RunResult(abstain_reason='other') instead of propagating exceptions.
Switching the default context from fork to spawn and accepting optional caller-supplied multiprocessing contexts preserves the never-raise contract while enabling thread-safe operation.
